dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product asks questions that are answered with several controls: which of these, one of these, these settings; an address in five fields. The set needs one name, a word that says whether it must be answered, a line that says how, and one reason when the answer as a whole is refused; and its members need one distance between them, stacked or in a row, that is the same in every form.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything the frame around a set of controls reads: the label's text style and the distance from the label and its description to the first control; the requirement tag's distance from the label, the asterisk's gap, and which mark a required set gets where the group does not say; the text style of the description and of the error text and their gaps; for each spacing (controls, fields) the distance between two members stacked; the distance between two members in a row; and the colors of the label, the description, the error text and the asterisk, plain and under the error condition (error.), at rest and while the group is disabled.
rules: A field group names a set of controls and lays them out: checkboxes or switches (spacing controls), or fields that belong together, such as an address (spacing fields). One control with a label above it is a field; a set of radio buttons is a radio group, which draws this frame from these tokens.
The label, the asterisk and the supporting text have the values of the field's tokens of the same names. Change them together in a layer.

The requirement tag is a small Tag — filled for required, tonal for optional — and nothing of it is here: it is styled by comp.tag.*, with every other small tag, and is drawn the same while the group is in error or disabled. requirement.mark follows sys.behavior.requirement-mark, as the field's does: set the sys token to change every form at once, requirement.mark only to mark sets differently from single fields, and requiredMark for one set.
The description sits under the label, before the controls, and stays while the group is in error; the error text sits below the controls, where a field's error text sits.
gap.fields and gap-inline are also the distances between two fields of a form that are in no group: a form's own stack reads them.
The group never selects, moves focus or holds a value, and each control keeps its own tokens.
The error color is for the error text alone. The controls show the error with their own error condition where they have one.
The group draws no container, no hover and no press answer, so it has no state layer: there is nothing for one to mix into.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a legend and a column of controls by hand.

typescale.$description: The group's label: the style of a field's label, because it does the same work for a set.

gap.$description: Distance between the label's last line, or the description's where there is one, and the first control: a field's distance between its label and its control.

mark.$description: How a required set is marked beside its label when the set does not say (FGR-6). tag: a small filled Tag holding requiredText. asterisk: "*" after the label. none: no mark; the requirement is still exposed. Follows the system's choice, as the Field's comp.field.requirement.mark does; a set's requiredMark prop overrides it. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product marks the required answers of all its forms in one manner, and the system-wide choice gives it; the field group must be able to leave it, because a mark above a set speaks for several controls: a product whose single fields carry an asterisk may still say "Required" in words above a set of checkboxes or radio buttons, or mark no set at all where each set shows that one of its options must be chosen.

gap.$description: Distance between the label's text and the requirement tag: where the tag stands is the frame's; what the tag looks like is the Tag's (comp.tag.*).

asterisk-gap.$description: Distance between the label's text and the asterisk: it belongs to the word it follows, closer than a tag stands.

typescale.$description: The description and the error text.

gap.$description: Distance between the label's last line and the description: the two are read as one heading for the set.
Distance between the last control and the error text: a field's distance between its control and its supporting row.
Distance between two members that follow each other down the group, and between two lines of a row that wrapped; per spacing.

controls.$description: Between two selection controls: with their 40 containers it puts their marks 48 apart, so that each keeps a whole touch target of its own.

fields.$description: Between two fields: wider than any distance inside one field (8 under the label, 4 above the help), so that each field's label, control and help read as one block. Also the distance between two fields of a form outside any group.

gap-inline.$description: Distance between two members that stand side by side in a horizontal group: from the end of one control's label to the next control, wide enough that a label is read with its own mark and not with the next one; and between two fields in one row (a city and its postal code).

color.$description: The label: the surface's text color, stronger than the supporting text, because it names the set.
The description under the label: secondary text.
The asterisk of a required mark drawn as an asterisk: primary, the role a filled tag is drawn in, never the error color, because nothing is wrong yet.
The group's error text, below its controls: the error role, used for errors and nothing else.
The label keeps naming the set while it is in error; the error text and the controls themselves show the error.
The description stays as it is in error: it says how to answer, which is what the person needs now.
